transcript:
Meeting header
Date/Time: 2025-06-11 15:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Hannah Cole (Redwood CSM), Samantha Lee (Omega Bank - Head of InfoSec), Raj Patel (Omega - Cloud Architect), Tom Nguyen (Omega - Procurement), Maya Johnson (Omega - Legal), Ethan Brooks (Omega - IT Ops)

Auto-generated sections (may be imperfect)
Summary: Quick walkthrough of SIG questionnaire items called out by Omega: encryption, key management, SOC 2, RBAC, SSO, audit logs and data residency. Discussed evidence attachments and timelines.
Action items: see metadata list.

Transcript body:
00:00 Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We are seeing a lot of names on the call so I appreciate you blocking time. Today's goal is to walk through the SIG questionnaire you sent and call out where we can attach evidence and where we need clarifications. Marco and Hannah from our side will cover the technical and customer success bits.
00:18 Samantha Lee: Thanks Lena. Quick ask up front: we're under a pretty tight vendor risk window, need most evidence to our portal within seven business days ideally.
00:24 Lena Park: Understood. We'll prioritize SOC 2 Type II and encryption docs. Marco, do you want to take the KMS bit?
00:32 Marco Diaz: Sure, yeah. So high level, Redwood supports both hosted key management and customer-managed KMS via integrations. For hosted API customers we typically use Redwood-managed keys by default — those are AES-256 at rest with envelope encryption. For Dedicated/Private we can integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, Google KMS, Azure Key Vault) and we support BYOK patterns and HSM-backed keys.
00:58 Raj Patel: Quick clarification — by "integrate" do you mean Redwood stores the customer key material, or you call the customer's KMS for every decrypt operation? We need zero key storage in Redwood.
01:10 Marco Diaz: Yeah great question. For the customer-managed flow we do not persist plaintext keys. We store key references/ARNs and call the customer's KMS for unwrap operations. There is a hybrid flow too — for latency-sensitive hosted customers we offer a delegated key caching option but that is only with contractual controls. If strict zero-storage is required we recommend Dedicated or Private with KMS integration.
01:42 Samantha Lee: Can you point me to documentation for the delegated caching controls — we need to show our risk team the mitigation controls.
01:47 Marco Diaz: We'll share the KMS key rotation policy excerpt and delegated cache controls after the call. adding to action items.
01:55 Tom Nguyen: Procurement note — any change to standard EULA for KMS or HSM usage? Also licensing for Dedicated?
02:03 Lena Park: Procurement questions are definitely something our contracts team will pick up; we'll flag the Dedicated licensing terms and share a redline-ready document.
02:12 Maya Johnson: From legal — we also need to confirm that Redwood will provide SOC 2 Type II report and if there are any carve-outs.
02:20 Hannah Cole: Yes, we can provide SOC 2 Type II. We'll attach the most recent report. There are no material carve-outs for the controls relevant to data security.
02:28 Samantha Lee: What's the date range for that report?
02:31 Hannah Cole: Last audit period ended 2025-03-31; report will be for the preceding 12 months.
02:37 Samantha Lee: Good. That helps.
02:40 Raj Patel: On network-level controls and segmentation — Omega requires that customer data reside in a dedicated VPC peering or private deployment for certain regulated workflows. What are the options?
02:51 Marco Diaz: We offer three deployment modes: Hosted API (public), Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity with isolated GPU pools and VPC integration), and Redwood Private (customer-controlled control plane, on-prem options). For strict data residency and network isolation we recommend Dedicated with VPC peering or Private depending on air-gapped needs.
03:10 Ethan Brooks: If we go Dedicated, can we enforce egress restrictions and route logs to our SIEM?
03:16 Marco Diaz: Yes, Dedicated supports customer-managed network controls including NAT/Egress rules, VPC peering, and private endpoints. We can also push audit logs and token-level events to customer endpoints—CloudWatch/Splunk/Datadog — or a secure S3 bucket with proper IAM.
03:33 Samantha Lee: What about retention on those logs? We need 12 months for certain audit trails and 7 years for others.
03:41 Marco Diaz: We can configure retention as part of the Dedicated deployment. Hosted customers have a default retention policy (90 days for granular request logs, 12 months for aggregated usage metrics) — but Dedicated allows customization to meet regulatory needs. We'll share the retention config doc.
03:58 Tom Nguyen: On the SIG: there are a number of evidence asks for configuration screenshots and policy excerpts. Are screenshots permissible or do you provide formal artifacts?
04:08 Hannah Cole: We generally provide a mix: a link to the SOC 2 attestation, policy extracts (password policy, incident response, change mgmt), and redacted screenshots or architecture diagrams for network segmentation. For sensitive configurations we provide a notarized attestation and can host a live review with our security team.
04:28 Samantha Lee: For KMS evidence we need proof of rotation and who has access to perform key management ops.
04:34 Marco Diaz: We'll provide the key rotation policy excerpt and operational roles. For RBAC we use role-based access controls within our IAM service and we integrate with SSO/SAML for user provisioning; we'll include a role mapping document and sample audit logs showing role changes.
04:53 Raj Patel: Do you support SCIM for provisioning? We prefer automated user lifecycle via SCIM.
04:58 Marco Diaz: Yes — Redwood supports SCIM for user provisioning and SAML 2.0 for SSO. We also support OIDC in certain flows. We can provide a sample SAML metadata file and SCIM configuration guide.
05:14 Samantha Lee: On encryption in transit — is everything TLS 1.2+? We require TLS 1.2 minimum, ideally TLS 1.3.
05:21 Marco Diaz: TLS 1.2 is enforced and TLS 1.3 is supported end-to-end; we use modern ciphers and have periodic vulnerability scanning. We'll include our TLS config and scanning cadence documentation.
05:33 Ethan Brooks: Does Redwood offer FIPS endpoints or FIPS-certified modules for customers who require them?
05:38 Marco Diaz: We don't currently expose FIPS endpoints for hosted customers, but for dedicated/private deployments we can support FIPS-validated modules depending on the environment and contractual requirements. That will require an architecture review.
05:52 Samantha Lee: Another common ask: can logs be exported with PII redaction or pseudonymization? We want logs to be useful for debugging but not carry raw PII in long-term storage.
06:04 Marco Diaz: We have configurable log scrubbing and redaction pipelines; by default request-level logs redact user-input fields flagged as PII, and we can run an additional pseudonymization step before long-term retention. We'll share the log-redaction whitepaper.
06:20 Tom Nguyen: Procurement timeline — if we accept Redwood Dedicated, what's typical lead time to get a dedicated pool and VPC set up?
06:27 Lena Park: Typical lead time is 4–8 weeks depending on capacity and region; with a prioritized enterprise onboarding we can accelerate some steps. We'll coordinate with your infra team to scope network requirements.
06:40 Samantha Lee: On the SIG form there's a question about incident response and breach notification timelines. We need to confirm notification within 72 hours.
06:48 Hannah Cole: Our incident response policy commits to 72-hour notification to customers for incidents impacting integrity/confidentiality of customer data. We'll attach the incident response playbook summary.
06:58 Raj Patel: Does Redwood provide penetration test reports or third-party scan attestations?
07:04 Hannah Cole: Yes, we have annual pen tests and we can provide executive summaries and remediation artifacts. Full reports are shared under NDA — if you want the full test we'll route through legal.
07:16 Maya Johnson: We'll likely request the full test under our mutual NDA.
07:20 Lena Park: Noted. We'll coordinate an NDA exchange after this call.
07:25 Samantha Lee: A few SIG-specific items: CAIQ answers around privileged access management, background checks, and vendor screening. Can you confirm?
07:34 Hannah Cole: We perform background checks for roles with privileged access and have PAM controls through our internal admin tooling — we'll include a high-level PAM diagram and HR policy excerpt.
07:45 Samantha Lee: For the evidence files, what's the preferred delivery method? Upload to our vendor portal or provide a secure link?
07:52 Lena Park: We can upload to your portal if you provide an endpoint, or we can provide time-limited secure links (S3 presigned) and also upload to the signup in your vendor sys. We'll confirm after the call.
08:03 Tom Nguyen: One last procurement question — do you have cyber insurance details we can share? Limits, carriers, that sort of thing.
08:11 Hannah Cole: Yes we have cyber insurance; we'll provide the certificate of insurance and policy limit summary.
08:17 Samantha Lee: Great, that will close a lot of gate questions.
08:22 Raj Patel: On data residency: Omega must keep EU customer data within EU regions for certain products. Does Redwood have EU-only deployments?
08:31 Marco Diaz: We do. Redwood operates in multiple cloud regions and can provision Dedicated capacity in EU regions. For strict residency we recommend a Dedicated or Private deployment pinned to the EU region. We'll provide region availability and latency profiles.
08:46 Samantha Lee: Any differences in encryption or KMS setup for EU regions?
08:50 Marco Diaz: No functional differences; the main change is the KMS endpoints and the ARNs. For customer-managed KMS you'll provision keys in the EU region and we will reference the regional KMS endpoints.
08:59 Maya Johnson: Does your SOC 2 report include controls for cross-border data transfer? We need to make sure there are no compliance gaps.
09:06 Hannah Cole: The SOC 2 scope includes data handling and transfer controls; we'll pull the specific control language from the report and attach.
09:12 Samantha Lee: On supplier risk — are any of your critical sub-processors located outside EU for EU-customer data?
09:19 Marco Diaz: Subprocessors vary; we maintain a subprocessors list and will provide a redacted list for review. For EU data we can architect Dedicated to minimize cross-border subprocessors but some low-level infra services may be global — we'll flag specifics.
09:36 Raj Patel: We need to run a small proof: can Redwood run an onboarding test where we send a sample file and we verify that logs show no plaintext retention after 24 hours? That's part of our risk validation.
09:46 Lena Park: We can run a scoped POC for that — Marco, would that be feasible as a short technical POC?
09:51 Marco Diaz: Yes, we can set up a short POC. We recommend a short checklist: 1) agree dataset (no real PII), 2) run sample queries, 3) capture request logs, 4) verify retention and scrubbing after 24h. We'll support with a runbook.
10:08 Samantha Lee: Great. Please include that in the next steps.
10:12 Lena Park: Noted — will add to next steps and action items.
10:16 Tom Nguyen: For the SIG cell on encryption key custody, can you provide a short diagram of the key flow? That will help our review team.
10:25 Marco Diaz: We'll attach an encryption topology diagram showing envelope encryption, KMS calls, and optional HSM flow.
10:31 Samantha Lee: One last technical question — do you use KV cache or any in-memory caches that might persist request prefixes? We worry about caches storing customer inputs.
10:41 Marco Diaz: The runtime uses a KV attention cache for model performance. For hosted flows we persist KV caches only for the duration of the request or session and do not store user prompt content long term. For dedicated/private we can configure cache flushing policies and avoid persistent caches. We'll include cache behavior docs and how to flush caches on session end.
11:03 Samantha Lee: Thanks. That's helpful.
11:07 Hannah Cole: I'll summarize deliverables: SOC 2 Type II report, KMS rotation policy excerpt, encryption topology diagram, log retention configuration, SCIM/SAML configuration samples, pen test NDA process, subprocessors list, and POC runbook. Anything else?
11:27 Samantha Lee: Also incident response playbook summary and cyber insurance cert.
11:31 Hannah Cole: Adding those.
11:33 Lena Park: Perfect. Let's do the follow-up cadence: we'll upload documents by 2025-06-12 and schedule an evidence review for 2025-06-18. Does that timeline work?
11:43 Samantha Lee: Yes, fits our window. Procurement still needs to confirm contract timelines but this helps.
11:48 Tom Nguyen: We'll review once evidence is in portal. If everything matches we'll move to the contracting step.
11:54 Maya Johnson: We'll prepare an NDA for pen test report access.
12:00 Lena Park: Thanks everyone. We'll circle back via email and post the links. If there are urgent items ping me directly.
12:07 Samantha Lee: Thanks — appreciate it.

End of transcript.

References / attachments mentioned: SOC2-Report.pdf (to be shared), KMS-key-rotation.pdf (to be shared), encryption-topology.png (diagram), log-retention-config.docx, SCIM-SAML-samples.zip, pen-test-NDA-template.docx
